results.correct_value: Glacier route best in late spring / early summer (roughly May-July); the ridge line is the late-summer/fall alternative
results.evidence: The direction is settled by two sources: the Northeast Shoulder route listing calls it a very good early-season climb (May-June), and the peak's route summary says the Kindy Ridge line uses the Snowking Glacier/snowfield in spring and early summer and the west ridge in late summer and fall. That supports season (May-Jul), gear and pro_tips, and contradicts best_season, seasonal_guidance (August 'optimal', optimalWindow mid-July to early September), itinerary.cal and approach_variants[0].season (June-September), climate.summer, seasonal_hazards.crevasses ('best traveled once well-covered (mid-summer)') and the avalanche block ('N/A' because the window is Jul-Sep). Aligning them needs new month-by-month guidance for May and June and a real avalanche entry for an early-season approach, which no source supplies month by month; that is a rebuild, not a minimal patch. No patch.

The live row changed since the earlier passes: the trailhead pin now sits at the FS 9070 left-fork road end at 4,254 ft and the crag pin at 4,650 ft, so the row's own waypoints now show ~400 ft of net rise against gain_ft 750 (the ground heights, ~4,250 ft at the road end and ~4,670 ft at the crag, agree). But net relief is only a floor for cumulative gain, so 750 is not provably wrong, and no published source states the approach gain for the Silver Basin / Citadel crags (area pages give only the 20-30 minute walk). A gain figure from pin heights would be computed. No patch.
